title: RFC: Cleanup of array_length, g_ptr_array_len, and "sizeof arr / sizeof arr[0]"
description:
There are several definitions of `g_ptr_array_len` and `array_length` scattered
around, and there are some files which include `epan/proto.h` or `epan/packet.h`
just for those definitions alone.  Some of these definitions are slightly
different from others.  Plenty of code computes a compile-time constant array
size using "sizeof arr / sizeof arr[0]" or similar, where the macros would be
more readable and less susceptible to error.

This sequence of three commits is somewhat invasive but makes a robust step
towards tidying this up.  There is still plenty more to be done.

I've posted it as an "RFC", but I have no objections if it is committed as-is;
I am just wary that this might be overstepping and might not be the preferred
approach for this cleanup.

As always, feedback is welcome.

notes.body:
Hi

May be add a note also on doc ? (README.Develloper ?)

Hmmm.  I'm not really finding a suitable location in `README.Developer` to put it.  There are existing mentions of how to declare arrays (Line 384 onwards), but that is in the "Portability" section and describes how to avoid platform-specific compilation failures, and guidance on using `array_length` doesn't seem to be a good fit there.

But perhaps we do not need to document it?  Once `array_length` is used throughout the codebase, we can hope that folks will use it in new code simply because it is visible and universally available. :smile:

> No attempt has yet been made to address expressions of the form "sizeof arr /
sizeof (TYPE)"; These would probably require manual handling to confirm that
the named TYPE indeed corresponds with the type of the array element.

I would be surprised if the TYPE is different than used in the array in this cases.

+/** @file
+ * Utility functions/macros for handling arrays, C and/or glib.
+ *
+ * Wireshark - Network traffic analyzer

+#ifndef __WSUTIL_ARRAY_H__
+#define __WSUTIL_ARRAY_H__
+
+/** Useful when you have an array whose size is known at compile-time. */
+#define array_length(x)	(sizeof (x) / sizeof (x)[0])
+
+/** glib doesn't have g_ptr_array_len, of all things! */
+#ifndef g_ptr_array_len
+#define g_ptr_array_len(a)      ((a) ? (a)->len : 0)
+#endif
+
+#endif /* __WSUTIL_ARRAY_H__ */

commits_data.title: Replace all "sizeof x / sizeof x[0]" with array_length.
commits_data.message:
Replace all "sizeof x / sizeof x[0]" with array_length.

A "sed" script was used to replace all occurrences of "sizeof arr / sizeof
arr[0]" (including one pair of brackets surrounding the whole expression, if
present, and including brackets around the argument to "sizeof", if present)
with an "array_length(x)" macro invocation.

A handful of more complex cases were manually edited.

The resulting code should be identical -- with the exception of a few trivial
details such as __LINE__ values and the precise formatting of assertion
messages.

No attempt has yet been made to address expressions of the form "sizeof arr /
sizeof (TYPE)"; These would probably require manual handling to confirm that
the named TYPE indeed corresponds with the type of the array element.

commits_data.title: Consolidate array_length and g_ptr_array_len into a new header.
commits_data.message:
Consolidate array_length and g_ptr_array_len into a new header.

There are several definitions of g_ptr_array_len and array_length scattered
around, and there are some files which include epan/proto.h or epan/packet.h
just for those definitions alone.

The definitions have been moved to a new wsutil/array.h, existing definitions
removed, and #includes amended to suit.
